$comment: Atrium's classification of the event catalogue the gateway ANNOUNCES about itself (`hello-ok.features.events`, vendored as ../2026.7.2-beta.5/event-catalogue.json). One entry per announced family, no more and no fewer — `events-coverage.test.ts` asserts the BIJECTION, so vendoring a version whose catalogue grew turns CI red until someone classifies the newcomer. Same vocabulary as the field coverage beside it: `handled` carries `by`, `ignored` carries `why`, `gap` REQUIRES a `note` saying what is unsupported and what it costs. 2026.7.2-beta.5: carried forward from 2026.7.1 (all 30 families still announced, entries unchanged); the 14 families new in this tag enter as `gap` on the frame-discovery queue. The tallies live in `counts` below, DERIVED and asserted by the ratchet — three separate corrections rotted when they were prose.

connect.challenge.by: openclaw-client.ts handshake — the auth challenge that precedes hello-ok

agent.by: normalizer + run-manager — the run/tool/activity stream a turn is built from

session.operation.note: The reader exists, is correct and is covered by tests — but it is NEVER FED (`normalizer.ts`, "NOT CURRENTLY FED"). The event reaches only connections that called `sessions.subscribe`, and subscribing on the turn-serving socket cost conversation frames, proven by bisect on the live bench. Real cost: a GATEWAY-decided compaction has no observable cause; only the compactions Atrium performs label themselves. To be fed by the dedicated session-events connection when that is built.

shutdown.by: connection-end.ts — names the GATEWAY_RESTARTING cause instead of a bare socket close

cron.note: Atrium ships cron management and a cron calendar, but it reconstructs cron facts from a TOOL completion on the agent stream (core/cron-part.ts matches name==="cron" && phase==="completed") rather than reading this broadcast. Deriving state from a tool's output is strictly weaker than reading the event the gateway emits for it: a cron that changes outside a tool call is invisible.

task.note: Async task engagements are derived from run-id shapes on the agent stream (`<tool>:<taskId>:ok|error`, suffixed `:agent-loop` since 2026.8.1 — subagent-announce-delivery.ts:219,230). Since 2026.8.1 the gateway also wakes the requester session with a synthetic `announce:requester-settle:<agentId>:<sessionKey>:<childRunIds>` run (subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts:389) — no child key, classified apart by isRequesterSettleRun. The native `plan` stream is emitted on delivery runs as well (measured 2026-09-02), so `plan.advance` is inferred for `update_plan` only; `progress_card` replaces the whole card on every put (markdown-only drops the steps) and a `steps: null` result is read as a cleared plan; the plan stream itself carries `steps: []` for those calls (readProgressCardPlanInput: `steps ?? []`) and is materialized as an empty plan, not from this broadcast. A task whose lifecycle the agent stream does not narrate is not observed at all.

talk.mode.note: Atrium has a realtime talk mode, driven entirely through RPC methods (`talk.client.*`). The gateway's own mode broadcast is not consumed, so a mode change made anywhere else is not reflected.

talk.event.note: Same surface as talk.mode: the talk feature exists but its event feed is unread.

exec.approval.requested.note: A turn blocked on an exec approval is, from Atrium's side, a turn that has gone quiet. W5 deliberately limits itself to suspending the budget and NAMING the wait, and the approval UI is explicitly out of scope — but the request event itself is what would let Atrium name it, and it is not read.

exec.approval.resolved.note: The other half of the above: nothing tells Atrium the wait ended.

plugin.approval.requested.note: Same class as exec.approval.requested, for plugin trust prompts.

session.message.why: Message history is Convex-authoritative in Atrium; the reply content a turn depends on arrives on the `chat` stream. Reading this too would duplicate a record Atrium already owns.

session.tool.why: Tool phases a turn depends on arrive on the `agent` stream (tool.status). This broadcast feeds the upstream sessions view, not a turn.

sessions.changed.why: Session-list housekeeping for the upstream client's own list. Atrium drives its chat list from Convex and never renders the gateway's.

presence.why: Channel presence for chat surfaces (who is online). Atrium is not a chat client and no turn depends on it.

tick.why: Periodic clock broadcast carrying no turn state.

health.why: Gateway self-report. Atrium's own health surface polls `/health` on its schedule rather than following a broadcast, so liveness does not depend on frames arriving.

heartbeat.why: Turn liveness is enforced by the bridge's own recv deadline (lot 29) and by heartbeat RUNS, which the normalizer already refuses as answers. The broadcast adds nothing a turn depends on.

node.pair.requested.why: Node pairing is gateway-operator business, performed outside Atrium.

node.invoke.request.why: Node-to-node invocation. Atrium is a client of one gateway and never services these.

device.pair.requested.why: Device pairing is gateway-operator business, performed outside Atrium.

voicewake.changed.why: Wake-word configuration for a local voice surface Atrium does not host.

terminal.data.why: The gateway's terminal surface is a separate product feature; Atrium exposes no terminal and would have nowhere to render this.

update.available.why: Gateway self-update notice. Atrium's version awareness comes from the handshake's `server.version` and its own compat manifest, not from an update prompt.

chat.metadata.changed.why: Broadcast with an EMPTY payload and `dropIfSlow: true` (server-chat-metadata-lifecycle.ts) — a 'refresh your chat metadata' nudge for a client that caches the gateway's chat list. Atrium's chat list is Convex-authoritative and it never calls `chat.history`, so there is nothing to refresh.

controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed.why: Control-UI pull-request panel. Atrium exposes no such view and calls none of the GitHub surfaces.

device.pair.changed.why: Device-pairing lifecycle for the Control UI. Atrium's bridge device is paired once out of band (local-openclaw/pair.sh) and it does not react to pairing changes at runtime.

device.pair.setup.completed.why: Operator-facing notice that a pairing hand-off finished (device-pair-setup-completion.ts). Same reason as `device.pair.changed`.

device.pair.setup.deliveryUncertain.why: Operator-facing notice that replay is blocked while credential delivery is unknown. Same reason as `device.pair.changed`.

node.runnerInventory.changed.why: Node/runner inventory for the Control UI. Atrium is a gateway CLIENT, not a node host, and subscribes to no node inventory.

portal.changed.why: Worker-environment portals (server-worker-environment-startup.ts). Atrium calls no `worker.*` or `environments.*` method.

progressCard.changed.why: `{sessionKey, revision}` from the `progressCard.*` methods, which Atrium does not call. CHECKED because it could have replaced the plan card's feed: `update-plan` is still present upstream at 2026.8.1 (14 non-test files, same as 2026.7.1), so this is an ADDITIONAL surface, not a replacement.

session.sharing.evidence.why: Emitted by `sessions.sharing`, a surface Atrium does not call. The same code path emits `sessions.changed` right after, which Atrium already handles — so no state change is lost by ignoring this one.

skills.changed.why: `{reason}` broadcast when the gateway reloads its skills. Atrium neither lists nor invokes skills through the gateway protocol.

users.prefs.changed.why: Control-UI user preferences. Atrium owns its own user model in Convex and reads no gateway user preference.
